title: fix: coalesce comm_msg state updates within a flush cycle
description:
## Summary

Fixes #212 — ipyleaflet LayersControl losing track of layers when reactive effects do remove+add within a single flush cycle.

**Root cause:** When multiple reactive effects modify the same widget (e.g., `map.remove(old_layer)` then `map.add(new_layer)`), each trait change sends a separate `comm_msg` to the client. The intermediate states (e.g., "layers after remove but before add") cause race conditions in ipyleaflet's async JS layer management. The final map rendering was correct, but the LayersControl overlay list would lose entries.

**Fix:** State-update `comm_msg` messages (`method="update"`) for the same model are now merged within each flush cycle, sending only the final value of each changed trait. This is equivalent to wrapping every reactive effect in ipywidgets' `hold_sync()`, but applied automatically at the transport layer. Non-update messages (`method="custom"`) are still sent individually.

**Key changes:**
- `_comm.py`: Added coalescing logic in `_publish_msg` — first update for a `comm_id` registers an `on_flushed` callback; subsequent updates merge their state dict into the pending entry
- Buffer paths for overridden state keys are properly replaced during merges
- `comm_close` and non-update `comm_msg` messages are unaffected

## Test plan

- [x] 5 new unit tests covering: basic coalescing, cross-trait merging, buffer handling, non-update passthrough, independent coalescing per model
- [x] New Playwright test (`ipyleaflet_layer_update`) that verifies LayersControl stays consistent after remove+add cycles
- [x] All 90 unit tests pass

title: fix: Plotly jump on rerender in filling layouts
description:
Closes #208.

Plotly `FigureWidget` can perform an initial draw at its internal fallback height before resizing to the actual container height. In filling layouts, that allows the output to become visible at the wrong height and then visibly jump to the final size.

This PR fixes that by delaying reveal for Plotly outputs until Plotly's own resize cycle has completed.

## What changed

- Keep the existing widget implementation flow for non-Plotly widgets.
- Pass `widget_pkg` from the server render payload so the client does not need to infer whether a widget is Plotly.
- Add a small Plotly-specific helper module in `js/src/plotly.ts`.
- For Plotly outputs:
  - keep the output hidden,
  - wait for Plotly's initial render/afterplot cycle,
  - call `Plotly.Plots.resize(...)` directly on the graph div,
  - wait for the post-resize `plotly_afterplot`,
  - then reveal the output.

## Reviewer context

This is intentionally narrow. It is not a general refactor of widget readiness logic.

The bug is tied to Plotly's render sequence:
1. initial draw at fallback height,
2. `plotlywidget-after-render`,
3. resize,
4. repaint at the real container height.

The fix is to avoid revealing the widget between steps 1 and 4.

## Test coverage

- Add a self-contained Playwright regression that reproduces the Plotly reveal/resize issue without depending on `examples/plotly/app.py` or extra Python packages.
- Keep the existing Plotly rerender cleanup coverage.
- Add a unit test covering the new `widget_pkg` render payload field.

title: Bulk restore: replace per-widget comm_open with single manager state message
description:
## Summary

Replaces the per-widget `comm_open` initialization pattern with a single bulk `shinywidgets_manager_state` message per render output. This eliminates widget model registration races and reduces message count from O(N) to O(1) for complex widget trees.

## Problem

When rendering a widget with many children (e.g., an ipyleaflet `Map` with 50+ `Marker` layers), each widget in the dependency graph sends its own `comm_open` message to the browser. The client-side `handle_comm_open` is async — it loads the widget's JS module, then calls `new_model()` to register the model. If `renderValue` arrives before all child models are fully registered, the parent widget's deserialization fails with "widget model not found" errors because it tries to resolve `IPY_MODEL_<id>` references to children that don't exist yet.

The root cause is that model registration happens asynchronously on a per-widget basis, with no guarantee that all models in a dependency graph are registered before any of them begin deserializing cross-references.

## Solution

### Server side (Python)

**New module: `shinywidgets/_bulk_state.py`**

- `find_ipy_model_refs(state)` — Recursively walks a serialized widget state dict and extracts all `IPY_MODEL_<id>` references. Used to discover the full dependency graph.
- `build_manager_state(root_widget, widget_instance_map, remove_buffers, collect_deps)` — BFS traversal from a root widget through its dependency graph. For each widget: calls `_repr_mimebundle_()` (needed for plotly), serializes state via `get_state()`, base64-encodes binary buffers, and collects HTML dependencies (deduplicated by name+version). Returns a payload containing the full widget closure.
- `materialize_bulk_comms(state_entries, widget_instance_map, comm_manager, comm_class, widget_comm_patch)` — Creates `ShinyComm(emit_open=False)` for each widget in the bulk closure, registering them in the comm manager without sending individual `comm_open` messages. Sets `_shinywidgets_bulk_owned = True` on each widget.

**Modified: `shinywidgets/_comm.py`**

- `ShinyComm.__init__` gains an `emit_open: bool = True` parameter. When `False`, the comm is registered in the manager and marked as not-closed, but no `comm_open` message is scheduled. This is used by `materialize_bulk_comms` — the client will receive the widget state through the bulk message instead.

**Modified: `shinywidgets/_shinywidgets.py`**

- `_open_shiny_comm` (the per-widget reactive effect at priority 99999) now checks `getattr(w, "_shinywidgets_bulk_owned", False)` at the top. If the bulk path already claimed the widget, the effect self-destructs without sending a `comm_open`.

**Modified: `shinywidgets/_render_widget_base.py`**

- `_render()` now calls `await self._send_bulk_state(widget, session)` before returning the render result.
- `_send_bulk_state()` orchestrates the bulk path: builds the full dependency closure via `build_manager_state`, materializes comms via `materialize_bulk_comms`, serializes the payload, and sends it as a `shinywidgets_manager_state` custom message.

### Client side (TypeScript)

**Modified: `js/src/output.ts`**

- New `restoreManagerState(mgr, state)` function: iterates over all models in the bulk state payload, decodes base64 buffers (using `put_buffers` from `@jupyter-widgets/base`), creates a `ShinyComm` for each, and calls `mgr.new_model()`. The key correctness property: `new_model()` calls `register_model()` **synchronously before its first `await`**, so all model promises are registered in `manager._models` before any async deserialization begins. This means cross-model `IPY_MODEL_` references always resolve, regardless of iteration order.
- New `shinywidgets_manager_state` custom message handler: renders HTML deps first (so widget JS modules are loadable), then calls `restoreManagerState`.
- Existing `shinywidgets_comm_open` handler now uses an `openQueue` promise chain to serialize processing. This hardens the legacy path for widgets not handled by bulk restore (e.g., dynamically created widgets after initial render).

### Activation logic

The bulk path only activates when the root widget's comm is still an `OrphanedShinyComm` at render time. This happens when widgets are constructed **inside** `@render_widget` — the common pattern for complex widget trees:

```python
@render_widget
def my_map():
    m = Map(center=(51.47, -0.00), zoom=12)
    for loc in locations:
        m.add_layer(Marker(location=loc))
    return m
```

When widgets are constructed **outside** `@render_widget` (e.g., at server function scope), Shiny's reactive effects phase runs `_open_shiny_comm` before the output renders. By the time `_render()` executes, the widget already has a live comm, and `_send_bulk_state` returns early to avoid duplicate model registration on the client.

## Message flow comparison

**Before (per-widget):**
```
Server → Client: comm_open (widget 1)    ← via on_flush
Server → Client: comm_open (widget 2)    ← via on_flush  
Server → Client: comm_open (widget N)    ← via on_flush
Server → Client: renderValue {model_id}  ← flush batch
Client: handle_comm_open(1) → async load JS → new_model(1) → async deserialize
Client: handle_comm_open(2) → async load JS → new_model(2) → async deserialize  
Client: renderValue → get_model(root) → deserialize → resolve IPY_MODEL refs → 💥 race
```

**After (bulk restore):**
```
Server → Client: shinywidgets_manager_state {all models}  ← send_custom_message
Server → Client: renderValue {model_id}                   ← flush batch
Client: restoreManagerState → new_model(1), new_model(2), ..., new_model(N)
          ↑ all promises registered synchronously before any deserialization
Client: await Promise.all(modelPromises) → all models resolve
Client: renderValue → get_model(root) → ✅ all refs available
```

## Test plan

- [x] 19 new unit tests across `test_bulk_state.py` and `test_comm_transport.py` covering:
  - `find_ipy_model_refs`: empty state, flat refs, nested dicts, lists, mixed nesting, dedup, non-model strings
  - `build_manager_state`: single widget, child traversal, deep graphs, buffer encoding, dep dedup, missing refs, `_repr_mimebundle_` invocation
  - `materialize_bulk_comms`: comm creation + flag setting, missing widget handling
  - `_open_shiny_comm` bulk-owned guard
  - `ShinyComm(emit_open=False)`: registration without scheduling, send/close still work
- [x] All 104 existing unit tests pass
- [x] Pyright type checking passes (0 errors)
- [x] Ruff format/lint passes
- [x] All 7 Playwright integration tests pass (altair, bokeh, plotly rerender cleanup; ipyleaflet marker click + rerender; buffer transport round-trip; isolate context rendering)

title: Fix browser-to-server widget buffer decoding
description:
## Summary
- decode inbound browser-to-server widget `buffers` on the Shiny side before forwarding comm messages to ipywidgets
- add a minimal `anywidget` Playwright regression that exercises both binary trait updates and binary custom messages

Closes #151.

## Problem
`shinywidgets` already base64-encodes browser-originated widget buffers so they can cross Shiny's input transport. The missing piece was on the server side: we were doing `json.loads()` and forwarding the message directly to the widget comm, which left `msg["buffers"]` as base64 strings. `ipywidgets.Widget._handle_msg()` expects bytes-like buffers for both:

- `update` messages, where `buffer_paths` are used to reconstruct binary state
- `custom` messages, where buffers are passed through to `on_msg` callbacks

As a result, browser-originated binary state/custom traffic was not protocol-correct even though the browser transport layer was already trying to preserve buffers.

## Test Coverage
This PR adds a small `anywidget`-based Playwright regression so the test isolates the browser-to-server binary transport behavior directly.

## What This PR Changes
### 1. Decode inbound buffers on the server
In `shinywidgets/_shinywidgets.py`, messages coming from `session.input.shinywidgets_comm_send()` now pass through a small `_decode_comm_buffers()` helper before `comm.handle_msg(msg)`.

That helper:
- leaves messages without buffers unchanged
- base64-decodes string buffers
- wraps decoded buffers in `memoryview`, which is accepted by ipywidgets' existing buffer handling
- leaves non-string buffers untouched if they ever appear

### 2. Add browser-to-server buffer regression coverage
`tests/playwright/buffer_transport/` adds a self-contained `anywidget` app and Playwright test that exercises both paths:

- normal synced trait update carrying binary state
- custom message carrying binary buffers

The server side reports the received payloads via Shiny text outputs so the test can assert the actual Python-visible state.

## Important Protocol Nuance Captured By The Test
The regression intentionally checks two different behaviors:

1. **Trait update path (`model.set(...); model.save_changes()`)**
   Even though the widget view creates a sliced `DataView`, upstream ipywidgets frontend logic collapses `ArrayBufferView` values to their full backing `ArrayBuffer` during normal state-sync serialization. So the correct observed value here is the full backing buffer: `00000UPDATE000` (`14 bytes`).

2. **Custom message path (`model.send(..., buffers=[...])`)**
   This path preserves the explicitly supplied sliced `Uint8Array`, so the correct observed value is just `CUSTOM` (`6 bytes`).

That distinction is important for review: this PR fixes the browser-to-server buffer transport boundary, but it does not change upstream ipywidgets serialization semantics for synced trait updates.

title: Fix issue #215: stabilize heavy ipyleaflet rerenders

title: fix: avoid plotly rerender swap transient double roots
description:
## Summary

This PR fixes a Plotly `FigureWidget` rerender issue where the output briefly contains two direct `.lm-Widget` roots during a rerender swap.

That transient double-root state is enough to make Plotly measure against the wrong layout state, which matches the rerender jump/flicker described in issue `#208`.

## Changes

- serialize widget render work per output element so rerenders do not overlap on the same container
- mark previous widget roots as stale before mounting the new view
- keep stale roots out of layout while teardown finishes
- strengthen the Playwright regression so it samples the transient DOM state during rerenders instead of only checking for cleanup errors afterward

## Why this is narrow

This does not change widget comm ordering or teardown semantics.
It only changes how a rerendered output container swaps visible widget roots during `renderValue()`.

title: fix: preserve child widget comm ordering for ipyleaflet updates
description:
## Summary
- delay `shinywidgets_comm_msg` until the reactive flush completes so child widget `comm_open` messages arrive before parent state updates that reference them
- add a Playwright regression based on the minimal `ipyleaflet` marker-click repro from #211
- add `ipyleaflet` to test dependencies for the new browser regression

## Why
The failing case is a parent widget update that introduces child widgets during the same flush. On current `main`, the browser can receive the parent `shinywidgets_comm_msg` before the child widget models exist client-side, which causes the first click marker update in `ipyleaflet` to be dropped and triggers the `state_change` error reported in #211.

This change keeps the client-side ordering consistent by sending mutation messages on `session.on_flushed(...)`, matching the point where newly created child widget comms have already been published.

## Additional context
During review, I checked this against Jupyter's comm model. In the reference Jupyter stack, `comm_open` creates the client-side comm/model first, and later `comm_msg` traffic assumes that comm already exists. JupyterLab's kernel connection also documents that kernel messages are handled in the order they are received, and that async handling pauses later message processing until the current handler completes. This change is therefore aligning Shiny's delivery timing with the ordering the Jupyter widget protocol already expects, rather than introducing a new assumption.

I also validated the issue outside the original `ipyleaflet` repro: on `main`, a parent widget update that introduces new child widget models can lag by one interaction in plain `ipywidgets` containers as well; with this change, those child models are available client-side before the parent mutation is applied.

Fixes #211
Related to #215

Closes #223

## Motivation

Re-rendering a widget output replaces the previous widget view with a new one. In practice, that teardown path could produce client-side cleanup noise during repeated rerenders, including errors like `Widget is not attached` and `no comm channel defined`.

The underlying problem is that some widget views need extra teardown before the model is closed, and some view cleanup code tries to sync state changes after the comm has already been torn down. That makes rerender behavior noisy even when the replacement itself succeeds.

## What This PR Changes

This PR hardens the client-side widget close path used during rerender:

- guards against models that do not have a `views` collection
- runs explicit view teardown for views that expose `destroy()`
- marks the model as no longer comm-live before `close()` so view cleanup does not try to sync `_view_count` over a dead comm
- suppresses only the two known teardown-noise patterns this PR is addressing, while continuing to log unexpected teardown failures
- triggers `comm:close` so the HTML manager releases its model reference

## Scope

This is a targeted rerender/teardown hardening change. It does not redesign the widget lifecycle or change how widgets are rendered when teardown is already clean.

It should also not be read as a full fix for the broader child-view failure discussed in `#215`. In local repros, this change removed the teardown-noise error but did not eliminate a separate `state_change` failure in an ipyleaflet-like reload scenario.

## Test Coverage

This PR adds Playwright regression coverage for repeated rerender across multiple widget types:

- plotly
- altair
- bokeh
- ipyleaflet

Each test verifies that repeated rerender leaves exactly one rendered widget in the output and does not emit the known teardown errors. The Playwright suite is also wired into GitHub Actions on Python 3.12.

## Reviewer Notes

The most important code is the `shinywidgets_comm_close` handler in `js/src/output.ts`. The key behavioral change is the ordering around teardown: perform any view-specific cleanup first, mark the comm inactive, then close the model and release the manager reference.

title: fix: Use render output's Context for widget cleanup instead of current Context
description:
## Summary

- Fixes widget cleanup registering on a temporary `reactive.isolate()` Context instead of the render output's Context, which caused premature `widget.close()` when upstream reactive sources invalidated
- `WidgetRenderContext` now captures the render Context at `__enter__` time and exposes it via `get_render_context()`
- `init_shiny_widget` uses the captured render Context for `on_close` registration instead of `get_current_context()`

## Root Cause

When a widget (e.g., `FigureWidget`) is constructed inside `reactive.isolate()`, `get_current_context()` returns the temporary isolate Context. When `reactive.poll` or any upstream reactive source fires, it invalidates this temporary Context, which triggers `on_close()` → `w.close()`, destroying the widget before the browser renders it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `examples/model-score` in py-shiny renders both Plotly charts correctly with streaming updates
- [ ] Verify that widgets created outside `reactive.isolate()` still clean up properly on re-render
- [ ] Verify that widgets created inside `reactive.isolate()` are only cleaned up when the render output re-executes, not when the isolate Context is invalidated

Closes #221

title: Allow for the `model_id` property to still be accessed after the widget is closed
description:
This problem was first discovered via https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinywidgets/issues/174

Here is a small reprex of the problem.

```python
from ipyleaflet import Map, Marker
from shiny import reactive
import shiny.express

from shinywidgets import render_widget

map = Map(zoom=2)

@render_widget
def map_out():
    reactive.invalidate_later(1)
    marker = Marker(location=(0, 0))
    map.add(marker)
    return map
```

After the 1st invalidation, you'll get:

```python
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'comm_id'
```

This happens because `.add()` reads of the `.model_id` property of every `Widget` instance (i.e., `Marker()`) that has ever been added to it. And, in recent versions of shinywidgets, we now `.close()` widgets when the reactive context they were initialized in get invalidated. When a widget gets closed, normally reading `.model_id` will result in error since that property reads `.comm.comm_id`, but `.comm` is `None`.

The workaround here is come up with a "mock" comm object that we add after close that allows for the `.model_id` property to still be read.

title: Ensure a session context is present when widgets are closed
description:
Closes #170

The reason this didn't come up in testing is because I was using an app that used `invalidate_later()` for invalidation, and it that case, the session is actually present `.on_invalidate()`. Whereas, if a reactive effect gets invalidated in the normal way, it apparently doesn't exist at `.on_invalidate()` time. 

This seems like a bug in Shiny, but since this is such a bad regression in shinywidgets, I'm gonna do this patch fix for now:

```python
from shiny import reactive
from shiny.express import input, ui
from shiny.reactive import get_current_context, invalidate_later
from shiny.session import get_current_session


@reactive.effect
def _():
    invalidate_later(1)

    # Prints the session, as expected
    ctx = get_current_context()
    ctx.on_invalidate(lambda: print(get_current_session()))


ui.input_action_button("btn", "Print session")


@reactive.effect
def _():
    input.btn()

    # Prints None?!?
    ctx = get_current_context()
    ctx.on_invalidate(lambda: print("Button click: ", get_current_session()))
```

title: Make output_widget compatible with Shiny modules
description:
## Repro

In `location.py`:

```python
from typing import Optional
from shiny import Inputs, Outputs, Session, module, reactive, render, req, ui
from shinywidgets import output_widget, register_widget, reactive_read
import ipyleaflet as L

# ============================================================
# Module: location
# ============================================================


@module.ui
def location_ui() -> ui.TagChildArg:
    return ui.div(
        output_widget("map"),
    )


@module.server
def location_server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):
    map = L.Map(center=(52, 360), zoom=4)
    register_widget("map", map)
```

In `app.py`:

```python
from shiny import Inputs, Outputs, Session, App, reactive, render, req, ui

import location

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    location.location_ui("location")
)


def server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):
    loc = location.location_server("location")



# The debug=True causes it to print messages to the console.
app = App(app_ui, server, debug=True)
```

title: Restore jQuery/$ directly instead of using noConflict() since the latter doesn't preserve event handlers
description:
A follow up to #38

Notice how, in this example, if you show the table, then change the slider the table renders again (while it's still hidden). Turns out this is because the `noConflict()` approach to restoring jQuery destroy's `shiny.js`'s event handers (to send output visibility when shown/hidden):

```py
from shiny import *
from ipyshiny import *
import ipywidgets as ipy

import seaborn as sns
import qgrid

iris = sns.load_dataset("iris")


app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.navset_tab(
        ui.nav("Slider", output_widget("s")), ui.nav("Widget", output_widget("widget"))
    ),
)


def server(input: Inputs, output: Outputs, session: Session):

    s = ipy.IntSlider(
        value=7,
        min=0,
        max=10,
        step=1,
        description="Test:",
        disabled=False,
        continuous_update=False,
        orientation="horizontal",
        readout=True,
        readout_format="d",
    )

    @output(name="s")
    @render_widget()
    def _():
        return s

    @output(name="widget")
    @render_widget()
    def _():
        print("Render widget: ", reactive_read(s, "value"))
        print("Is hidden: ", input[".clientdata_output_widget_hidden"]())
        return qgrid.show_grid(iris)

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

title: Don't bundle/source libembed twice
description:
Closes #22

After spending lots of time trying to figure how why:

https://github.com/rstudio/ipyshiny/blob/ea98ce5c3206cb50af9417c5f19af846d6f90f5f/js/src/output.ts#L75-L81

was updating the server-side state, but not the client-side display, I eventually noticed that the `callback` provided to:

https://github.com/rstudio/ipyshiny/blob/ea98ce5c3206cb50af9417c5f19af846d6f90f5f/js/src/comm.ts#L74-L76

was different on initial load vs the last server-side change. And that was happening because the ipywidget dependencies are first sourced here

https://github.com/rstudio/ipyshiny/blob/ea98ce5c3206cb50af9417c5f19af846d6f90f5f/ipyshiny/_dependencies.py#L44-L49

and we were also bunding them in the `output.js` dependency

https://github.com/rstudio/ipyshiny/blob/ea98ce5c3206cb50af9417c5f19af846d6f90f5f/ipyshiny/_dependencies.py#L54-L59

By not bundling the dependencies, we not only fix #22, but also reduce the size of `output.js` by quite a lot.

description:

Changelog

Sourced from pip's changelog.

21.1 (2021-04-24)

Process

  • Start installation scheme migration from distutils to sysconfig. A warning is implemented to detect differences between the two implementations to encourage user reports, so we can avoid breakages before they happen.

Features

  • Add the ability for the new resolver to process URL constraints. ([#8253](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8253) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8253>_)
  • Add a feature --use-feature=in-tree-build to build local projects in-place when installing. This is expected to become the default behavior in pip 21.3; see Installing from local packages <https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/#installing-from-local-packages>_ for more information. ([#9091](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9091) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9091>_)
  • Bring back the "(from versions: ...)" message, that was shown on resolution failures. ([#9139](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9139) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9139>_)
  • Add support for editable installs for project with only setup.cfg files. ([#9547](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9547) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9547>_)
  • Improve performance when picking the best file from indexes during pip install. ([#9748](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9748) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9748>_)
  • Warn instead of erroring out when doing a PEP 517 build in presence of --build-option. Warn when doing a PEP 517 build in presence of --global-option. ([#9774](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9774) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9774>_)

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed --target to work with --editable installs. ([#4390](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/4390) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/4390>_)
  • Add a warning, discouraging the usage of pip as root, outside a virtual environment. ([#6409](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6409) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/6409>_)
  • Ignore .dist-info directories if the stem is not a valid Python distribution name, so they don't show up in e.g. pip freeze. ([#7269](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7269) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/7269>_)
  • Only query the keyring for URLs that actually trigger error 401. This prevents an unnecessary keyring unlock prompt on every pip install invocation (even with default index URL which is not password protected). ([#8090](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8090) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8090>_)
  • Prevent packages already-installed alongside with pip to be injected into an isolated build environment during build-time dependency population. ([#8214](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8214) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8214>_)
  • Fix pip freeze permission denied error in order to display an understandable error message and offer solutions. ([#8418](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8418) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8418>_)
  • Correctly uninstall script files (from setuptools' scripts argument), when installed with --user. ([#8733](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8733) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8733>_)
  • New resolver: When a requirement is requested both via a direct URL (req @ URL) and via version specifier with extras (req[extra]), the resolver will now be able to use the URL to correctly resolve the requirement with extras. ([#8785](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8785) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/8785>_)
  • New resolver: Show relevant entries from user-supplied constraint files in the error message to improve debuggability. ([#9300](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9300) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9300>_)
  • Avoid parsing version to make the version check more robust against lousily debundled downstream distributions. ([#9348](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9348) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9348>_)
  • --user is no longer suggested incorrectly when pip fails with a permission error in a virtual environment. ([#9409](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9409) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9409>_)
  • Fix incorrect reporting on Requires-Python conflicts. ([#9541](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9541) <https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/9541>_)
